source.title: Masked and Predictive Self-Supervised Pretraining for Brain MRI: Effects of Objective Design on Disease Detection
source.authors: E. Ergün; H. Chandarana; Daniel K. Sodickson; Gozde Unal

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures representational similarity and reports that it varies with objective, downstream task, depth, and adaptation. It does not test convergence with scale, but its results refine the scope of representational alignment.
record.gate_note: The CKA analyses bear on representation alignment. Downstream disease-classification scores, clustering metrics, and spectral-power comparisons are not rows for these claim versions. The study does not sweep model scale or capability, compare vision and language models, or test independently initialized seeds.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (3D brain MRI SSL), the study compares representations of four same-architecture, same-data ViT-Base encoders trained with different objectives (MAE, SL-MAE, JEPA, VCR-JEPA). It uses pairwise linear and RBF CKA before and after fine-tuning. This bears on V7 (partial, objective-driven alignment) and on V6 (kernel and input dependence of the measured similarity). It does not test scale, modality, seeds, mapping or shared features.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the pretraining paradigm (reconstruction vs latent prediction) establishes characteristic, distinct representation geometries, which auxiliary objectives modify modestly. Fine-tuning then reshapes these geometries depending on depth, objective and task, and reduces agreement between objectives without erasing the family differences. VCR-JEPA preserves the broadest cross-task alignment. They state that persistence at larger scale is untested.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses CKA to compare representation geometry across objectives, tasks, and training stages; it does not implement a scale-based convergence test.
record.method_sensitivity: Representational similarity varies with objective, downstream task, depth, and fine-tuning stage. Linear and RBF CKA are both presented, but their relative results are not described in text.

fits_no_version.finding: Pretrained-to-fine-tuned CKA within each encoder declines with depth, depending on task and objective. Cross-task CKA between two fine-tunes of the same encoder is broadest for VCR-JEPA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning reorganizes a model's own representation geometry in a depth-, objective- and task-dependent way (representational drift/reuse under adaptation).

record.problems: Primarily ViT-Base-scale encoders; no model-scale or capability sweep. ADNI uses five-fold cross-validation, while other cohorts use fixed subject-level partitions. CKA plots are reported without uncertainty estimates, and the text does not explain whether the RBF-kernel results differ from linear CKA. Cross-study comparisons are acknowledged as uncontrolled.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream classification, clustering, and spectral-power results are omitted because they do not measure the representation-alignment claim versions. Other CKA plots describing internal layer organization are not separately rowed because the extracted rows capture the reported alignment comparisons relevant to V6 and V7.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep. Architecture and data are held fixed (single ViT-Base 3D).
No vision–language or paired cross-modal comparison.
No models differing only in random seed.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation tests.
No unit, feature or circuit-level comparison.
No neighbour-count (mutual-kNN) settings and no out-of-distribution input test; the RBF bandwidth is fixed at 0.4×median.
No scale plateau test. Shared training data is held constant, so a data cause cannot be separated from an objective cause.

missing.what: Input/cohort dependence: the same pretrained checkpoints evaluated on different ADNI cohorts give different pairwise CKA. Examples: MAE–VCR-JEPA 0.64 (AD cohort) vs 0.71 (MCI cohort), MAE–SL-MAE 0.92 vs 0.95. The authors note the differences arise from the evaluation cohort. This is a V6 input-dependence row.

Layer-wise baseline vs auxiliary-objective CKA (MAE vs SL-MAE, JEPA vs VCR-JEPA) under both linear and RBF kernels. Pretrained pairs are highly aligned across depth; fine-tuned pairs show a mid-layer drop.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not framed around the convergence hypothesis. Its cross-objective CKA is a narrow test: one architecture, one data mixture, a small 3D MRI model. Tranche changed from T5 to T3, since the study gives a result in a new setting rather than an argument against a version. Figures 8 and S3 numbers were read from the extracted text; panel ordering differs between Fig. 8 (a pre-AD, b ft-AD, c pre-MCI, d ft-MCI) and Fig. S3 (a pre-AD, b pre-MCI, c ft-AD, d ft-MCI). No uncertainty is reported for CKA.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep; no test of convergence among independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
No paired image-caption or vision-language representation comparison.
No comparison across random initializations or analysis of shared features or subspaces across seeds.
No test of mapping, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.

The study compares linear and RBF CKA and evaluates representations on different task cohorts, but does not test neighbor-count settings or out-of-distribution effects; the text does not state a specific linear-versus-RBF outcome.

The study reports objective- and task-dependent CKA alignment, but does not test whether alignment plateaus with scale or whether shared training data/objectives, rather than a common model of reality, cause the alignment.

rows.subject: MAE, SL-MAE, JEPA, and VCR-JEPA (pairwise aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Pairwise linear CKA of final-layer representations across objective variants

conditions.value: ADNI NC vs. AD and NC vs. MCI evaluation cohorts

rows.measure: Pairwise CKA; the authors report that within-family similarity (MAE–SL-MAE; JEPA–VCR-JEPA) exceeds cross-family similarity on both cohorts.
rows.baseline: Cross-family comparisons are the reference for the reported within-family comparison; numeric baseline not stated in the text.
rows.value: Within-family similarity consistently exceeds cross-family similarity; numeric values are shown in Figure 8.
rows.note: Aggregate statement across the reported encoder pairs; the authors describe objective-dependent representation geometries, not universal convergence.
rows.check: Values are readable from Fig. 8. Pretrained linear CKA within-family is 0.92 (AD cohort) and 0.95 (MCI cohort). Cross-family is 0.61–0.74 (AD) and 0.63–0.76 (MCI). So alignment across objectives is incomplete and higher when objectives are shared. Data and architecture are held fixed, so a data cause cannot be assessed. Its V6 link concerns cohort dependence, which belongs in a separate row (see missing).

source_check.correct: Figure 8 supplies numeric values. Pretrained within-family CKA: MAE–SL-MAE 0.92 (AD), 0.95 (MCI); JEPA–VCR-JEPA 0.74 (AD), 0.76 (MCI). Cross-family CKA: 0.61–0.72 (AD), 0.63–0.71 (MCI). The qualitative ordering is correct.
source_check.locator_found: Section 6.5, Figure 8(a,c), and the paragraph immediately following Figure 8.
source_check.problem: The numeric-unavailability characterization is incorrect; the verdict fix also includes within-family JEPA–VCR-JEPA values in the cross-family ranges.

rows.subject: MAE, SL-MAE, JEPA, and VCR-JEPA (pairwise aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Pairwise linear CKA before and after downstream fine-tuning

conditions.value: ADNI NC vs. AD and NC vs. MCI

rows.value: Pairwise similarity generally decreases after fine-tuning, particularly for NC vs. AD; within-family versus cross-family organization remains evident.
rows.note: The text reports an aggregate pattern; numeric pairwise values are presented in Figure 8.
rows.check: Fig. 8 values: after fine-tuning, cross-family CKA drops sharply. MAE–JEPA goes 0.72→0.23 (AD) and 0.68→0.34 (MCI); SL-MAE–JEPA goes 0.64→0.19 (AD). Within-family drops too (MAE–SL-MAE 0.92→0.67). Shared downstream supervision reduces rather than raises cross-model alignment. This is not a metric or input choice, so the V6 link is removed.

rows.subject: MAE, SL-MAE, JEPA, and VCR-JEPA (aggregate by objective)
rows.operation_detail: Layer-wise CKA between each pretrained encoder and its fine-tuned counterpart
rows.baseline: Pretrained representation compared with its task-fine-tuned counterpart
rows.value: Similarity generally decreases with depth; NC vs. AD shows a sharper transition to low similarity in later layers than NC vs. MCI. VCR-JEPA retains substantial pretrained alignment deeper into the encoder, particularly for NC vs. AD.
rows.note: The study interprets CKA as extent of representational adaptation, not its causal origin.
rows.check: Compares each encoder with its own fine-tuned checkpoint. That measures adaptation of one model, not convergence between independently trained models. It is not a measure for any version.

rows.baseline: Other compared objective variants; numeric baseline not stated in text.
rows.value: VCR-JEPA exhibits the broadest cross-task alignment across early and intermediate layers in both task-pair comparisons; alignment can diverge in later layers.
rows.note: Authors characterize this as representational reuse across related tasks, not a direct measure of predictive performance.
rows.check: Cross-task CKA between two fine-tunes of the same pretrained encoder. That measures representational reuse within one model lineage, not convergence across independently trained models.

rows.subject: MAE and JEPA (pretrained and fine-tuned comparisons)
rows.operation_detail: RBF-kernel CKA robustness analyses alongside linear CKA

conditions.value: ADNI NC vs. AD and NC vs. MCI

rows.note: The supplement supplies RBF-kernel plots, but the text does not describe whether the RBF results differ from the linear-kernel results.
rows.check: Not figure-only: Fig. S3 gives numbers. RBF pretrained AD values are MAE–VCR 0.74 (linear 0.64), SL-MAE–VCR 0.71 (0.61), JEPA–VCR 0.82 (0.74). Fine-tuned AD values: MAE–SL-MAE 0.58 (linear 0.67), VCR pairs about 0.1 lower. Magnitudes shift by up to about 0.1 with the kernel, but the within- versus cross-family ordering is preserved. Subject should be all four encoders, not only MAE and JEPA. Figs. S1–S2 layer-wise RBF results are figure-only.

source_check.correct: Figure S3 prints pairwise RBF CKA values for all four encoders. For AD, pretrained MAE–VCR-JEPA is 0.74 versus linear 0.64; SL-MAE–VCR-JEPA is 0.71 versus 0.61; JEPA–VCR-JEPA is 0.82 versus 0.74. Fine-tuned AD MAE–VCR-JEPA is 0.33 versus linear 0.45, a difference of 0.12. RBF bandwidth is 0.4 times the median pairwise Euclidean distance.
source_check.locator_found: Section 6.5 kernel definition; Supplementary Section S2.3 and Figure S3; Figure 8 for linear comparisons.

relationships.condition: Same architecture and pretraining data, different SSL objectives; pretrained and fine-tuned final-layer CKA on ADNI cohorts
relationships.reason: Cross-objective CKA is far from complete (0.61–0.76 pretrained, 0.19–0.45 fine-tuned). Encoders sharing an objective family align more (0.92–0.95) (CKA01, CKA02).
relationships.display_finding: Cross-objective CKA was 0.61–0.76 before fine-tuning and 0.19–0.45 afterward, compared with 0.92–0.95 for encoders sharing an objective family.
